statement: The compact-open centralizer of a transitive nonabelian orientation-preserving homeomorphism group of a line or circle is free, proper and discrete. It is trivial or infinite cyclic on a line and finite cyclic on a circle. For every such intrinsic orbit of a plane-loop group, the actual operator stabilizer image is therefore already closed and discrete and gives a genuine regular covering of the orbit, with its original restriction kernel retained.
depends_on: C26 Polish open orbit-map theorem; C28 intrinsic orbit topology and operator restriction; C30 normalizer/evaluation construction and properness proof, applied in dimension one; C33 verified Hilbert--Smith product-action input; one-manifold covering classification
manuscript_passages: Section 23, folios 140-141, scans 279-281; Part C(b) infinite-operator request; exact one-dimensional operator-image reduction at the boundary remaining in C.12
depends_on_doubtful_reading: None. The centralizer topology is intrinsic compact-open topology, and the operator stabilizer, its image, its kernel, and the actual covering quotient are all specified.
notes: The closed normalizer quotient identifies the full centralizer with a closed subset of the line or circle and makes its action free and proper. A positive-dimensional centralizer would be a transitive one-dimensional Lie group, forcing the original transitive group to lie in its abelian translation centralizer. Nonabelianness therefore makes the centralizer discrete. The quotient covering gives the exact cyclic classification. Every actual operator image is a subgroup of this discrete group, hence already closed and proper; its source restriction kernel remains explicit. No continuity of restriction from an inherited plane topology to a recurrent intrinsic line topology is asserted, and no transverse continuity or extension across X2 is supplied. C12 remains Open.
